mathematical_scope: 10 unittest methods across exact residual, reversible Haar, and spectral/support classes. Tests include small direct DFT comparisons, same-helper FFT comparisons, symbolic butterfly identities and numerical scaled unitarity.
input_and_guard_coverage: Valid-domain fixed parameter pairs dominate; no malformed input/group tests. Basis tests sample four columns rather than all N. Numerical tests in the final class import NumPy unconditionally. Most implementation invariants are asserts rather than unittest assertions, so optimized Python can weaken coverage.
cost_and_scaling: Small exact direct DFT and sparse oracles are quadratic or worse with exponentiation; numerical make_R plus Gram and tests can be cubic. Large N=2^30 case only evaluates cost formulas, not a transform.
test_evidence: Textual count is 7 methods before line 79 and 3 after. unittest.main normally calls sys.exit, so direct python tests/test_phase15.py registers only the first 7; discovery imports the whole module and can collect all 10. validate.py uses discovery, so its chosen launch route avoids this particular omission.
dependency_identity: Assigned executor/coherence/unitarity_probe/complexity_budget/sparse_green_gate hashes; NumPy version unpinned. Test file inserts its package root ahead of sys.path.

findings.finding: The unittest.main call appears before SpectralAndSupportGates. Direct invocation silently omits all three final tests: scaled unitarity, symbolic large costs and sparse-inverse support bound. Move the main guard after all class definitions in any repair.
The independent FFT test shares fft_radix2 with the implementation; it does not isolate shared root/sign/arithmetic defects. Direct-DFT tests provide some separate coverage.

acceptance_boundary: Accept complete static read and intended discovery coverage, not a 10-test direct-run claim or proof that any tests passed.
